name: Hypotrichosis-Osteolysis-Periodontitis-Palmoplantar Keratoderma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Hypotrichosis-Osteolysis-Periodontitis-Palmoplantar Keratoderma Syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital or early-onset sparse scalp hair (hypotrichosis)
Progressive osteolysis, especially of distal phalanges and clavicles
Severe early-onset periodontitis leading to premature loss of teeth
Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: hypotrichosis, osteolysis, and early-onset periodontitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in the MMP2 gene can support diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive osteolysis of distal phalanges and clavicles
searchTerms: bone loss in fingertips and collarbones
progressive bone destruction in hands and shoulders
gradual bone disappearance in distal bones

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe early-onset periodontitis with premature tooth loss
searchTerms: early tooth loss from gum infection

common.symptomName: Palmoplantar keratoderma (thickening of skin on palms and soles)
searchTerms: thick skin on palms and soles
hardened skin on hands and feet

common.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia
searchTerms: unusual facial features with prominent forehead and flat midface

occasional.symptomName: Recurrent skin infections secondary to keratoderma
searchTerms: frequent skin infections due to thick skin
skin infections caused by thickened skin

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during active periodontitis
imaging: Radiographic evidence of osteolysis in distal phalanges and clavicles
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in MMP2 gene (matrix metalloproteinase 2)
other: Histopathology of skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis in palmoplantar regions

distinguishingFeatures: More extensive carpal and tarsal bone involvement

redFlags: Early-onset severe periodontitis with rapid tooth loss
Congenital hypotrichosis with associated skin and bone abnormalities
references: OMIM Entry - 610018: Hypotrichosis with Osteolysis and Periodontitis
Miyamoto et al., 2007. MMP2 mutations cause multicentric osteolysis with arthritis and hypotrichosis. Nature Genetics.
